key_insight: A 20-qubit trapped-ion QPU can supply small-cluster expectation values accurate enough for NLCE+QA to estimate thermodynamic-limit energies and quasiparticle dispersions, but only if nonlinear post-processing remains stable under noise.
engineering_relevance: This shows a practical path for near-term quantum hardware to contribute to many-body materials and condensed-matter calculations via cluster-based thermodynamic extrapolation.
method: NLCE+QA: numerical linked-cluster expansion combined with quantum subroutines to extrapolate thermodynamic-limit observables.
PCAT block-diagonalization: projector-based transformation used to extract effective cluster quantities.
Hardware workflows tested with adiabatic state preparation (ASP), variational quantum eigensolver (VQE), and a CX-test readout alternative.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports numerical evaluations on a 20-qubit trapped-ion processor for TFIM settings in 1D, ladder geometry, and longitudinal field cases, comparing what current hardware can support after classical post-processing.
watch_item: Matrix inversion and square-root steps in PCAT amplify measurement noise, so the approach is sensitive to readout precision and may fail if hardware errors are too large.
paper_title: Thermodynamic-limit dispersion relations on trapped-ion quantum hardware
